feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid public-sector experience. It reads well and shows progression, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some structure/style inconsistencies that reduce punch.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression at NACo into director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale and credibility signals: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms strengthen impact.  
- Relevant, modern positioning: Drupal, analytics stack, AI-enabled search, workflow automation, and multimedia production align well with senior digital platform roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and make the CV feel sharper.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially in freelance and earlier roles; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or cost/time savings.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings found, but the footer project list is cramped and reads more like portfolio copy than CV content.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps with competencies and experience bullets; adding one concrete scale marker would sharpen impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce the long list of functions; emphasize leadership scope and outcomes.
- Add one concrete signal of scale/relevance from recent work (for example, enterprise web modernization for high-volume public-sector platforms).
- Use parallel wording and hyphenation consistently: “AI-enabled,” “public sector” or “public-sector” consistently across the CV.

Possible rewrite:
Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web and communications ecosystems. Leads enterprise website strategy, digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models,” “content operations,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” repeat heavily from Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Enterprise web modernization” is echoed in recent NACo and consulting experience; keep the intro high-level rather than listing every capability.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with slightly tighter wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify longer items for faster scanning.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia.
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve “operations” and “systems” language here, and keep tools/platform names in Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled…experiences,” and “multimedia production” repeat language already used in the header.
- This section also overlaps significantly with Topline Skills; consider trimming one of the two sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use a cleaner list format with parallel verbs and tighter phrasing; e.g., “Designed,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched.”
- Add one concrete outcome or distinguishing detail per project where possible, especially for AI Hybrid Search and the microsite.
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently, and spell out “10 x 20-foot” for readability.
- Consider this rewrite: “Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and scalable modular architecture. Organization Anniversary Campaign — Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series — Produced a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with recent consulting and NACo experience bullets.
- “Built” appears repeatedly; vary verbs to avoid monotony.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project section. Make it sharper by emphasizing ownership, platform outcomes, and 2–3 concrete wins.

Suggested edit
- Open with a stronger lead: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 focused points: platform/campaign build, systems/workflows/analytics, governance across channels, AI search initiative.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/templates launched, users supported, workflow time saved, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/engagement improvements, stakeholder teams served.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting” with “built and maintained Drupal features, front-end components, and fixes for high-traffic public web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI-enabled search, microsites, and anniversary/campaign work are already echoed in Recent Projects; keep this entry at the leadership/outcomes level.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the summary and NACo role—show what changed or improved here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening line were more concise and if channel oversight bullets emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the intro with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Rephrase channel bullet to show results if available: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials; add engagement, list growth, or campaign performance metrics if you have them.”
- Combine operations/analytics language for concision: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video leadership overlaps with the earlier NACo role; keep this version focused on building the in-house studio, not recurring video production.
- Email/social oversight also appears in prior NACo entries; emphasize enterprise leadership here rather than day-to-day execution.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth before the broader strategy/governance scope of 2022–2024.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcome language where possible: “Launched/expanded a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel” and, if available, include views, open rates, production volume, or engagement growth.
- Rephrase vague bullets with ownership: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams” and “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency and turnaround time.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; distinguish this as scaling/operationalizing the series, not originating it.
- “Workflows/governance” overlaps with the Director role; keep this version tactical rather than enterprise-level.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies and reads generic rather than differentiated. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership themes most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “campaign platform strategy” if you want stronger alignment with the 2024–present consulting work.
- Keep terms at the leadership level; avoid wording that sounds tactical since technical execution is already covered elsewhere.
- If space allows, use “enterprise web governance” instead of “editorial systems” for clearer connection to the Drupal migration and publisher model.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems/governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint

- CMS modernization

- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-signal or dated items like “jQuery” unless directly required for target roles.
- Group similar items to improve scanability: platforms, modernization, implementation, integrations, AI/search.
- If possible, tie to scale in adjacent experience rather than here; this section should stay concise and strategic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, API integrations, Airtable systems” are already repeated in Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; keep the strongest phrasing in one place.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize business impact and decision support.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”

- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and dashboarding across GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity”
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented phrase tied to recent work: “used to improve reporting clarity and strategic decision-making”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization”
- Avoid listing every analytics tool here if they already appear in Technical + IT

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more specific to senior-level delivery capability, not just task-level tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Tighten and elevate phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production**
- If you want stronger impact, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: **Built and operated in-house studio workflows for advocacy programming and live events**
- Keep only 4 items max; remove “editing” if space is tight, since production already implies it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”).
- “Studio operations” and PTZ systems are already supported by the Director of Digital Media bullet about building NACo’s in-house studio.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the same tools already listed under “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This section should either add specificity on level/relevance or be trimmed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers to show depth without becoming a sentence: **Drupal (enterprise content platforms, migrations) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, align to recent impact: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one detailed version and make the other shorter or remove overlapping tools.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise focus of the CV; keep only if it supports a specific project or personal site strategy.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus toward execution: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Development & Deployment Tools.”
- Use cleaner, current phrasing: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- Consider grouping by function for readability: “Front-end: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery • Integration/deployment: APIs, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions • Tagging: Google Tag Manager.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to impact with examples rather than here: e.g., custom microsites, tagging/analytics setup, workflow automation, or lightweight serverless integrations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; keep it in one place or shorten one version.
- “API integrations” and automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and “Automation & Workflow Systems.”

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant systems first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop lower-value or older/general tools unless actively used recently: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a raw list: **Airtable systems, workflow automation, project tracking and team collaboration using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack and Microsoft Teams**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases in multiple sections.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar category signals; listing all four can feel padded.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too generic and misses the scale/context shown in recent NACo work. It should signal enterprise email operations rather than read like a basic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** _(enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations, audience engagement workflows)_
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses: _(supported newsletters reaching tens of thousands of public-sector stakeholders)_ to connect directly to recent impact.
- Keep naming consistent and concise: use official product names once; avoid slashes if possible, e.g. **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys**.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform experience first, based on actual usage depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies and email leadership already described in NACo roles; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- If Higher Logic or Mailchimp were minor/older-use tools, consider dropping one to avoid diluting stronger enterprise platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the stronger “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills section. In Technical + IT, it should read more like a concise tools stack and avoid broad capability terms.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to platform/tool names only; move capability terms like “SEO,” “A/B testing,” and “Dashboarding” to Topline Skills or a project bullet.
- Reorder by strongest/recently evidenced tools: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity”
- If space allows, make one capability more specific: replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [3] (“Analytics, Insights & Optimization”); consider merging or differentiating one as tools vs. one as capabilities.
- “Dashboarding” repeats the reporting/infrastructure language already established in recent NACo experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” and team-building contributions without repeating later leadership claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around concrete outputs: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics or metrics if available: event audience size, video cadence, traffic lift, email/social growth, or number of livestreams produced.
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored” if not a formal manager.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the “first podcast” achievement and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities.”
- Add the clearest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten the multimedia clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audience, stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with stronger, impact-oriented multimedia claims already made in recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize tools/software rather than broad production capabilities already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast editing/production • Livestream control room workflows”
